clue.text: And the rest still in bed, cryptically?

indicators.note: the question mark and 'cryptically' tell the solver the word for lying abed must be read the other way, up the down light

parts.note: someone still in bed at noon is up late, a lie-in

explanation.surface: A question about whether everyone else is still asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' signals that LATE, the lie-abed word, is entered backwards, reading up the column to give ET AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is the Latin abbreviation meaning 'and others', used to cut short a list of names.

indicators.note: doing something irregularly means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar tip: use irregular verbs to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges USE VERBS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To subserve is a formal verb meaning to promote or be of use to a purpose, a synonym of help.

clue.text: Group which may be on the up?

indicators.text: which may be on the up?
indicators.note: in a down light the name reads the same whether taken downwards or up, so it may be entered either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A pop group whose fortunes may be rising.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a palindrome, so written up the column it is unchanged; 'on the up' also hints at a pop group climbing the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA was the Swedish pop group that won Eurovision in 1974 with Waterloo.

indicators.note: the bone word sits inside the word for a male animal

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is men only
the shin is the shinbone, the tibia

explanation.surface: A man takes a beating, punished with a bone injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets hiding' reads like a beating, but stashing means hiding away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing something means storing it secretly, so it is a synonym of hiding as a present participle.

parts.note: B stands for second class, as in a B-list or B-team
ranks are positions in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A torture device used for second-rate places.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 27 is INSTRUMENT OF TORTURE. Branks, also called the scold's bridle, was an iron frame clamped on the head to silence a nagging woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The branks was an iron headpiece with a tongue gag, a historical punishment device and a kind of torture instrument.

parts.note: the comedian of 11-across was famous for deliberately playing the piano of 16-down badly, so his keyboard tortured listeners

explanation.walkthrough: Les Dawson's act featured deliberately off-key piano playing, so his piano is cast as a device that tortures listeners; the phrase is also the theme for several clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly played piano inflicts suffering on the ear, a comic picture of a device of cruelty.

clue.text: Rose has outdated hairdo to disguise

parts.note: a DA (duck's arse) is a slicked-back 1950s haircut
to mask is to disguise

explanation.surface: A rose with a retro hairstyle tries to hide itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The DA, short for duck's arse, is a greased 1950s hairstyle swept to a point at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is a fragrant old garden variety, so the word names a kind of flowering shrub.

clue.text: By the way, requests company gets 6 27

parts.note: a hitchhiker at the roadside thumbs a lift, requesting a ride
a crew is a ship's or film's company

explanation.surface: Asking for rides at the roadside, a group acquires a torture device.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 27 is INSTRUMENT OF TORTURE. 'By the way' means by the roadside, where hitchhikers stand with thumbs out.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumbscrew was a device for crushing the thumbs, used to extract confessions.

clue.text: 6's 8 managed to fill vale, reaching centre of brae

indicators.note: the word for managed is put inside the farewell word, filling it

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell, as is the British ta-ta
to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: the middle letters of the Scottish word for hillside are taken

explanation.surface: Music echoing through a Scottish valley as it reaches the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 6's 8 is instrument's call, from 6-down and 8-down. 'vale' looks like a valley but is the Latin goodbye, matching the British ta-ta.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarantara imitates a trumpet fanfare, so it is the call sounded by a brass instrument.

clue.text: Bundle of cash passed back in class for comic

indicators.note: the reversed money word goes inside the lesson word

parts.note: a lesson is a class at school

indicators.note: passing something back hands it in the reverse direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: A pupil secretly hands a roll of notes backwards during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like social class but is a school lesson; 'passed back' is the note handed backwards in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Dawson was a British comedian famous for deadpan jokes about his mother-in-law and his tuneless piano.

parts.note: the stammer-like t is simply the letter T
a rail is the track a train runs on

explanation.walkthrough: The 't-track' looks like a stutter, but the lone t is a letter put before RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or rough track, and also a set of marks left by someone passing.

clue.text: Doctor titters, having quickly noted passages

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician giggles while jotting down some passages in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges TITTERS; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti are passages in a fugue where entries of the theme overlap closely, so the notes come quickly.

indicators.note: the dropped-h word goes inside the urban word

parts.note: a town is an urban area
humiliated is humbled, here with the h dropped, as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated goes into a run-down part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''umiliated' shows a dropped H, so HUMBLED loses its H too, giving UMBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbledown describes a building falling into ruin, a synonym of dilapidated.

explanation.surface: A conceited person named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill is a poster, which may be stuck up on a wall; Bill also reads as a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill posted on a wall is stuck up, and stuck-up also means snobbish and arrogant, like hoity-toity.

clue.text: One's played with boy in river

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the river name

parts.note: the Po is the main river of northern Italy
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone plays with a lad in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's played' is the definition, and 'with' is a link; the boy sits inside the Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a keyboard instrument, something that is played.

clue.text: Watery fluid man put in drink

indicators.note: the pronoun is put inside the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit to drink
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man slips something into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' gives the pronoun rather than a chess piece or abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a thin watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Something to chew, sucker rolled around

indicators.note: rolling something round turns it about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker

explanation.surface: A gullible person rolls a sweet around their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled around' turns MUG into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is chewing gum, something kept in the mouth and chewed.

parts.note: I as an object becomes me
anti means against, so it stands for being opposed to or hating
myself is me

explanation.surface: A gloomy confession of self-loathing, at least for the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hate myself' is read as me anti me.
explanation.definitionFit: In the meantime means for the present, in the interval until something else happens.

indicators.note: turning back means the letters found are read backwards
the letters are found inside the words, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A girl metamorphoses into an African elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' hides ANELE across 'African elephant'; 'turning' reverses that to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a girl's name, the Spanish, Italian and Russian form of Helen.

clue.text: Will one's responsibility flower, given disruption of court?

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river; the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: disrupting something throws it into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Whose job is it to tend a flower if the court is disturbed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a thing that flows, the River Exe in south-west England; 'given disruption of' rearranges COURT into CUTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person a will names to carry out its provisions, so the will is their responsibility.

clue.text: Refuse collectors unable to conceive not finishing?

indicators.note: the last letter is left off, so the word is not completed

parts.note: a creature lacking a womb would be wombless, unable to have young

explanation.surface: Bin men who cannot have children never finish their rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry creatures in a British children's TV series who collect and recycle litter on Wimbledon Common. WOMBLESS loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wombles tidy up rubbish others leave behind, so they are jokingly collectors of refuse.

clue.text: In which one stands naked as exhibitionist?

explanation.walkthrough: One stands undressed in a shower; a shower is also one who shows things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is the cubicle people wash in unclothed, and also, read as show-er, someone who displays themselves.

indicators.note: modelling clay reshapes it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fashion model shows off a red coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' rearranges RED COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Irish house knocked over by Irish premier — it's a long story

indicators.note: the premier, first, letter of the word is taken
knocking something over turns it upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An Irish premier knocks down an Irish house: quite a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like the Taoiseach but just picks I from 'Irish'; 'knocked over' reverses DAIL to LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's lengthy epic poem about the Trojan War, a very long story.

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, Maggie to many, was nicknamed the Iron Lady
a maiden is an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A torture device named after the single Mrs Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 27 is INSTRUMENT OF TORTURE. Maggie is Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister called the Iron Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron maiden was a legendary spiked cabinet in which victims were enclosed.

explanation.walkthrough: 6 27 is INSTRUMENT OF TORTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack stretched victims' limbs; a rack of lamb is also a cut or joint of meat.

indicators.note: a lid is the top, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: A drain without its cover becomes a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without lid' removes the top, the first letter, from SEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed water jug.

clue.text: However badly lame, only odd characters drown

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged
only the first and third letters, the odd ones, of the word are used

explanation.surface: Even with a bad leg, only strange types can drown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only odd characters' takes LM from 'lame'; 'badly' rearranges HOWEVER with LM.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm is to submerge completely, as a flood drowns land.

clue.text: About to become bankrupt having invested a hundred — a near thing

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: the hundred is put inside the bankruptcy phrase, invested in it

parts.note: to lose all is to be ruined
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: About to go broke after investing a hundred, a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' gives C for circa, a common abbreviation on dates; 'having invested' puts the hundred into the bankruptcy phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is a narrow escape, a near thing.
